# Build and environment

For the ordinary persistent text OS, use [text-session instructions](text-session.md).
Plain `demo` now opens that session and reuses its owner disk. The explicit
diagnostic/service profiles described below retain their isolated test behavior.

Supported and tested P00 host: Windows 10 Pro x64 with Rust 1.94.1, MSVC linker
14.44.35228.0 and Windows SDK libraries installed. Rustup already has the host,
`x86_64-unknown-none` and `x86_64-unknown-uefi` targets, Clippy and rustfmt.
`profiles/build/p00.json` records the selected versions. Other hosts are not tested.

Run commands from the repository root. `cargo xtask doctor` captures real compiler,
linker and host probes in `reports/environment.json`. It reports absent later-phase
inputs without making them mandatory for P00. Missing host tools fail their command.
`link /?` prints its version but exits nonzero on this host; the report preserves
that fact. Actual host linking is established by the executable/test builds.

`cargo xtask verify` checks records, formatting, Clippy with warnings as errors,
host tests and the portable format crates against both guest targets. P01 also builds,
inspects and smoke-tests two independent host release executables, then compares
their complete hashes. Cargo.lock is required
and the command uses locked resolution. The initial dependency acquisition used
the existing Cargo cache, with `cargo generate-lockfile --offline`; no installer
or downloaded setup script was executed. A new machine needs the same Rust/SDK
inputs and permitted registry dependencies before running the commands.

P01 validates ELF/PE inputs and compiles portable libraries for guest targets.
P02 builds actual firmware/kernel/initfs through `build --profile dev-qemu-x64`.
While P12's qualification schema is unfinished, an explicit
`build --profile dev-qemu-x64 --through P11` builds the diagnostic foundation for
isolated development measurements. It does not change the active phase or run a
cumulative qualification gate.
Guest packages require explicit firmware/baremetal features and distinct targets;
host tests do not compile or execute guest entry points by default.
No workspace-wide default
target is set, so host tooling cannot accidentally become a guest executable.

QEMU 11.1.0 is owner-installed at `C:/Program Files/qemu`; OVMF code/vars were
downloaded from QEMU v10.2.0 commit `698104725efad4b29079d857dfdebbd804e34c99`.
The hardware profile pins absolute paths and hashes, pc-q35-11.1, qemu64-v1 and TCG.
`cargo xtask check-emulator` checks actual identities and capabilities. The doctor
uses these acquired profile paths or explicit `DOOR_OVMF_CODE` and
`DOOR_OVMF_VARS_TEMPLATE` paths and hashes their actual bytes. It never guesses
filenames or modifies firmware. Code and variable-template acquisition are checked
independently; either missing input remains a blocker. Providing paths does not qualify the hardware
profile: execution requires acquired provenance, machine/CPU versions and runnable topology.
TCG is the selected diagnostic accelerator; actual guest integration began in P02.
See `project/NEXT_STEPS.md` for the next gate.

Additional commands:

```powershell
cargo xtask plan --profile dev-qemu-x64
cargo xtask build --profile host-dev
cargo xtask inspect --class host target/debug/door-xtask.exe
cargo xtask image --manifest out/artifacts/image-inputs.json
cargo xtask run --profile profiles/hardware/qemu-diagnostic-x64.json --image out/images/<run-id>/image.json
```

Plan/build/inspect/image/run execute on real P02 inputs as well as host fixtures.
`out/latest-dev-image.json` points to the most recent inspected guest build. In P08,
plain `demo` selects the retained service-console image from a successful suite.
The cumulative suite also exercises the original diagnostic console.
`stop-demo` validates the saved QMP UUID
before stopping that VM. Prerequisite failures return nonzero. Read the
build/image and emulator contracts under `specs/contracts` for exact schemas.

Controlled builds scope path remapping and the pinned MSVC linker's observed
`/Brepro` option plus stable `/PDBALTPATH` to the host executable. Two real builds
matched byte-for-byte. This excludes clean-machine, guest and virtual FAT sector
reproducibility. Output directories and raw evidence are ignored, not source scripts.

P02's guest build uses `profiles/build/dev-qemu-x64.json`, the original kernel linker
script and sorted initfs manifest. Target flags are scoped to each subprocess:
freestanding static high-half kernel/no red zone; firmware `/Brepro` and `/debug:none`.
Firmware PDB identities varied across exclusive build paths; disabling that release
metadata establishes complete file repeatability without modifying generated bytes.
Unstripped kernel ELF symbols and per-build `kernel.map` are retained.

`cargo xtask test boot` performs two guest rebuilds and the selected phase's actual suite
plus H/D/R/P interactions/screens. The full P02 `verify` also runs host tests,
strict host/guest Clippy, portable target checks and persistent evidence validation.
The boot media is read-only virtual FAT attached through VirtIO, with private
variable state/image copies. It is not a native VirtIO driver or installable disk.

The historical P03 gate keeps the acquired 2 GiB/one-vCPU profile unchanged and adds the same pinned
machine/CPU/firmware at 256 MiB in `profiles/hardware/qemu-minimal-x64.json`.
The full phase suite executes twelve processes: six P02 cases, UD, double fault,
read-only/NX/guard faults and minimum-memory normal completion, followed by the
existing H/D/R/P demo. Both normal profiles initialize the real allocator,
guarded exception stacks, retained early heap and calibrated local APIC timer.
The kernel library's deterministic frame/heap/page-table/layout tests run on the
host; privileged instructions are exercised by the explicit guest binary.

ACPI tables come from the firmware configuration table before ExitBootServices,
with current memory-map bounds, checksums and copied platform facts. P03 requires
an ACPI PM timer and qualified only the discovered BSP; unsupported platform modes fail
initialization. The public Intel/ACPI acquisitions and their hashes are recorded
in `specs/sources/index.json`. No new build-time dependency or helper script is needed.

P04 preserves the one-CPU/256 MiB and one-CPU/2 GiB profile identities and adds
`profiles/hardware/qemu-smp2-x64.json` and `qemu-smp4-x64.json`. The selected suite
has fifteen cases: all twelve prior cases plus normal two/four-CPU execution and
deliberate missing-AP startup in the two-CPU profile. Each launch gets private
firmware variables, image copies, serial capture and an exact source/profile binding.

The firmware reserves two low pages for AP startup and publishes a checked startup
handoff. Original assembly in `kernel/src/arch/x86_64/ap_start.S` transitions the
secondary into the existing four-level address space; each observed CPU installs
its own descriptor and emergency-stack state. Context layout and assembly inputs
are part of source identity. `context.rs`, `interrupts.S` and `state_probe.S` implement
the actual context switch and architectural preservation tests. `kernel/src/task`
owns portable scheduler/wait metadata, `execution.rs` provides the IRQ-safe runtime
bridge, and `task_diagnostics.rs` supplies real kernel workers and mapping stress.

The profile enables the x87/SSE state preserved by its FXSAVE/FXRSTOR path. It does
not advertise AVX/XSAVE or infer arbitrary CPU-state support. The allocator remains
bounded to its P03 frame/heap/table capacities, with up to 16 task slots and four
online CPU slots. AP idle/emergency stacks and startup backing remain retained;
only actually retired worker stacks are released. Current guest fixture failure
modes and P04 console text are development diagnostics, not release payload.

P04 guest/demo execution, the full current-source gate and independent critic
acceptance passed. Use the status/phase ledger to select
the gate, and do not treat an earlier P03 report as P04 qualification.

P05 builds `door-native-fixtures` alongside each complete guest build.
`native-runtime` uses the N0 libraries; `native-probe` repeats ABI literals in
independent assembly. Both are inspected ELF executables with separate link maps,
small code model, static relocation, disabled red zone and `lto=off`. Generated
initfs entries resolve to those exact inspected bytes. Each reproducibility pass
records five artifacts: firmware, kernel, initfs, runtime fixture and raw probe.
Historical phase reports retain their original three-artifact contract.

`kernel/src/process` owns launch policy, VM lifetime and syscall integration;
`kernel/src/executive` owns portable handle/process/channel transactions. Private
user mappings share only supervisor kernel entries. Normal/minimum-memory/SMP/
degraded boots run P03 and P04 diagnostics before the protected native suite.
The framebuffer remains a development console through P05.

P06 adds a separate writable development disk in
`profiles/hardware/qemu-storage-x64.json`. Existing hardware profiles and the
read-only boot ESP remain unchanged. The selected gate keeps all fifteen P05
scenarios and adds `storage-write` followed by `storage-reopen`, then the console
interaction check. Both storage boots run P04/P05 before exercising the modern
VirtIO PCI block transport, GPT, FAT32, ext2, and the mount namespace.

The reusable formatter and independent byte auditor live in
`tools/xtask/src/storage`. They do not invoke host disk utilities or guest parser
code. Create and inspect a disposable image with:

```powershell
cargo xtask disk create
cargo xtask disk inspect --state initial out/storage/<session>/data.raw
cargo xtask run --profile profiles/hardware/qemu-storage-x64.json --image out/images/<build>/image.json --disk out/storage/<session>/data.raw --mode storage-write
cargo xtask run --profile profiles/hardware/qemu-storage-x64.json --image out/images/<build>/image.json --disk out/storage/<session>/data.raw --mode storage-reopen
cargo xtask disk inspect --state persisted out/storage/<session>/data.raw
```

Each creation exclusively creates `out/storage/<session>/`, retaining
`initial.raw`, `initial-audit.json`, and a writable `data.raw`. Writable launches
accept only a regular 128 MiB file at that exact workspace-relative shape;
traversal, links/reparse points, device paths, and arbitrary host paths fail.
The generated QEMU command attaches it through
`virtio-blk-pci,drive=door-data,disable-legacy=on,serial=DOOR-P06-DATA`, separately
from the firmware boot medium. Commands preserve their normal source snapshots,
prerequisite hashes, exact argument vector, serial bytes, and actual process exit.

The disk has 262144 logical 512-byte sectors. GPT primary/backup headers and entry
arrays describe a 64 MiB FAT32 partition at LBA 2048 and a 32 MiB ext2 partition
at LBA 133120. FAT32 uses one sector per cluster, 32 reserved sectors, two
1009-sector FATs, root cluster 2, and `HELLO.TXT` containing
`Door FAT32 exchange\n`. Ext2 uses 8192 4096-byte blocks, one group, 128 128-byte
inodes, and only the FILETYPE incompatibility bit. Blocks 0–9 and inodes 1–11 are
initially allocated; inode 11 contains `seed.txt` with `Door ext2 seed\n`.
These are original deterministic fixture bytes, not an imported filesystem image.

The guest creates `pending.bin`, writes 6000 bytes, patches 1024 bytes across
the 4096-byte boundary at offset 3584, renames it to `persist.bin`, observes the
updated bytes through an already-open identity, and flushes. Initial byte `i` is
`(i*37+11)%251`; patch byte `j` is `(j*13+7)%251`. The final CRC32 is `aaa29e86`.
The second QEMU process opens the same raw image and verifies those exact bytes.
The host independently checks both GPT CRCs/mirrors, FAT allocations/mirrors and
seed, ext2 bitmaps/free counts, directory records, reachable inode/block ownership,
final name, full file bytes, SHA-256, and CRC32. Each guest's `data-after.raw`
snapshot is retained and hash-bound to its report; the initial, write, reopen,
and final audit records must form one exact chain.

Only the ext2 partition and the explicit single-sector reset probe at LBA 200000
may change during the write boot. Reopen must preserve all bytes except that probe.
The probe submits an actual pending write during reset, so its completion timing
is not presented as a power-loss guarantee. Short-read/write and flush failures
use the guest's fault adapter around the real transport: partial metadata bytes
or a completed flush precede an injected error, then the filesystem must reject
further mutation until remount. Queue exhaustion, cancellation/reset, stale request
identity, and DMA retirement exercise the actual driver lifecycle. P06 checks
the remaining stack space sampled during every counted block-I/O callback while
filesystem frames are live: the original 128 KiB boot stack must retain at least
16 KiB at every sample. `DOOR_P06 STACK PASS` reports this sampled margin; it does
not claim an absolute instruction-by-instruction high-water measurement. P06 checks
clean flush/reboot persistence; journal replay, crash recovery, Windows file
semantics, and physical-device durability remain later work. See the storage
contract and ADR 0011 for the bounded filesystem policy.

P06 qualification requires its own exact report and critic digest, both storage
cases, numeric driver counters, negotiated features, cleanup markers, and fresh
independent audits of retained raw bytes. Removing a case, changing a payload,
substituting an older phase report, or retaining only serial success cannot pass.

P07 uses the distinct `qemu-persistence-x64.json` profile and formatter option
`cargo xtask disk create --profile p07`. Its original disk/partition GUIDs identify
the P07 fixture; FAT32/ext2 geometry remains the P06 geometry. A third 2 MiB GPT
partition at LBA 202752 contains two 4 KiB redo headers and up to 64 4 KiB payload
pages. `--profile p07-small` keeps the same partitions but constrains ext2 to
32 blocks for actual capacity exhaustion. Both variants retain initial raw bytes
and independent audits under a fresh `out/storage/<session>/` directory. Inspect
either with `cargo xtask disk inspect --state p07 <relative-data.raw>`.

The full P07 gate retains all seventeen P06 processes and adds eighteen:
save/reopen, five interruption/recovery/second-reopen sequences, and a dedicated
capacity run. The modes are `persist-save`, `persist-reopen`, `journal-prepare`,
`journal-commit`, `journal-first-home`, `journal-home`, `journal-checkpoint`,
`recover-old`, `recover-new`, `persist-old`, `persist-new`, and `persist-full`.
Use the same `run --profile ... --image ... --disk ... --mode ...` argument shape
as P06. The gate automatically clones the saved baseline into distinct private
branches before each interruption; manual runs leave that sequencing to the caller.

The saved note is 6000 bytes with byte `i=(i*37+11)%251` and CRC32 `01ea357b`.
One transaction changes it to `i=(i*19+23)%251`, CRC32 `69f67483`, renames
`/users/1001/note-Ω.txt` to `revised-Ω.txt`, updates its ACL, changes native
theme/scale from 1/125 to 2/150, and updates the separate typed HKCU registry
fixture from epoch 1 to 2. The unrelated `keep.bin` remains unchanged.
The versioned `door.catalog` file binds logical object identity to the ext2
inode/generation/volume and is committed in the same redo transaction as data.
The independent host auditor decodes that catalog, checks every backing-file
association and allocation, and compares all these fields with the expected state.

Interruptions use QEMU exit 37 and an exact per-run `JOURNAL_INTERRUPTED` token.
They happen after prepared payload flush, committed-header flush, the first home
page flush, all home-page flush, or checkpoint flush. The first point must retain
the old state; all committed points must recover the new state. Captured physical
home bytes must match that exact boundary. The host independently applies the
checksummed redo pages, compares the complete recovered home partition, verifies
both checkpoint copies, then requires a second reopen with identical raw bytes.
This tests the selected controlled interruption model and flush-capable QEMU disk;
it does not establish arbitrary physical-controller power-loss behavior.

The capacity variant commits nine 8192-byte `fullNN` files until all 32 filesystem
blocks are allocated, rejects another allocation, and checks retained contents and
zero leaked allocation after remount. The saved fixture separately exercises
replace-over-open, delete-pending lifetime, truncate and stale identities before
committing; freed inodes may retain only their generation tombstone. P06 fixture
bytes, profiles, original gates and retained evidence remain valid and distinct.

P08 uses `profiles/build/initfs-p08.json`, preserving the original initfs manifest
for historical evidence. Each guest build independently links `door-init`,
`door-storage`, `door-session` and `door-console` from `door-system-services`, plus
`native-workload` from its own application package. These join both P05 fixtures
inside the authenticated initfs. Two controlled builds compare all ten artifacts
(firmware, kernel, archive and seven native executables), with per-executable link
maps and exact target flags. No native standard-library port is implied by the
N2-foundation runtime designation.

The P08 private disk reuses the P07 GPT/ext2/journal formatter and original format
identities. `profiles/hardware/qemu-services-x64.json` retains the one-CPU, 2 GiB
TCG hardware and uses the separate `DOOR-P08-DATA` device serial. Commands are:

```powershell
cargo xtask disk create --profile p08
cargo xtask disk inspect --state p08 out/storage/<session>-p08/data.raw
cargo xtask run --profile profiles/hardware/qemu-services-x64.json --image out/images/<build>/image.json --disk out/storage/<session>-p08/data.raw --mode services-save
cargo xtask test services --image out/images/<build>/image.json
```

Service modes are `services-save`, `services-reopen`, `services-restart` and
`services-failure`. The cumulative harness owns fresh saved and corrupt branches;
manual launches must supply the corresponding disk state. Failure mode requires
the deliberately corrupted saved catalog, not an empty disk. Final cumulative gate
`host-1792060739947826700-17608` passed 281 host tests, all 39 guest cases, both
interactive checks and two matching ten-artifact builds with unchanged inputs.
The accepted `reports/critics/p08-critic.json` binds that report and all four C01–C04 fixes
with zero unresolved findings. P08 closure checks passed; P09 is active. Consult the phase ledger for the selected phase.

`test services` owns the save, reopen, restart and corrupt branches, then exercises
the native console with real QMP keyboard input and independent byte audits. It is
a reusable integration check during development; only the cumulative `verify` gate
can qualify P08. `demo --profile services --image <image.json> --disk <saved.raw>`
opens the native console using a private copy of a qualified saved disk. After a
successful cumulative P08 suite, plain `demo` selects that retained service image.

The release host orchestrator avoids debug SHA-256 overhead during repeated full
128 MiB image audits. Build it with `cargo build --locked --release --package
door-xtask` and invoke `.\target\release\door-xtask.exe verify`. Required checks,
timeouts, source snapshots and raw evidence are the same as `cargo xtask verify`.


## P09 Windows x64 artifacts

The selected P09 build adds original `ntdll.dll` and `kernel32.dll` plus an
independent Windows SDK C/MASM executable to `profiles/build/initfs-p09.json`.
The ordinary fixture imports only five kernel32 APIs. Its absolute data pointer
requires DIR64 relocation; the assembly probe checks Windows nonvolatile GPR and
SIMD preservation. The fixture is built twice using the pinned MSVC/SDK profile,
then the first executable runs on installed Windows without byte modifications.
Original DLLs are built separately without a CRT or Windows implementation code;
kernel32 links the generated original ntdll import library. The runner retains
compiler/linker commands, acquired SDK-header hashes, maps and import libraries.

`cargo xtask build --profile windows-reference` exercises the standalone reference
fixture; `windows-artifacts` additionally builds and validates the original DLLs.
`cargo xtask disk clone --profile p09 --from <saved-p08.raw>` creates a private,
independently audited disk. Run that disk with `qemu-windows-x64.json` and mode
`windows-basic` for an exploratory guest check. The cumulative `verify` creates
its own disk from the P08 save case and qualifies all 40 scenarios, both native
interactive checks, two matching thirteen-artifact builds, and the same-binary
reference comparison. Exploratory success does not close the phase.

P09 closed with final gate `reports/runs/host-1792150739645891100-11748/report.json`
(SHA256 `48fa8a34f832a2b5de8762d7de4deeb307de72b2e1c1a85ec40960c943bac1ad`).
310 host tests, all40 guest scenarios, both interactive checks and two matching
13-artifact builds passed with unchanged inputs. The exact independent Windows
EXE runs on Windows and Door with verified output/exit73, real relocation,
invalid handles/buffers and ABI preservation. Seven malformed-load cases and79
construction rollback points pass; process/DMA resources retire and the P08 disk
remains byte-identical. `reports/critics/p09-critic.json` accepts248 build inputs,1202
hash bindings and eight rejected weakened gates with zero unresolved findings.
The supported scope remains one no-CRT Windows thread, static original DLLs and
bounded synchronous ASCII output. P10 owns DLL/TLS/unwind and broader base APIs.
`cargo xtask build --profile windows-base` builds the independent P10 application DLL/EXE and measures Windows behavior. The selected P10 `dev-qemu-x64` image uses `initfs-p10.json` and includes both P09 and P10 fixtures. Run mode `windows-base` with the Windows hardware profile and a fresh private saved P08 disk clone for exploratory guest execution; use `windows-reopen` after its successful save. `cargo xtask verify` runs the complete cumulative qualification.


P10 implements the bounded Windows base profile described in
specs/abi/windows-base-p10.md. Its full gate extends inherited coverage to42 guest
cases, both interactive checks,16 reproducible artifacts, original P09 reference
comparison, P10 Windows reference and actual save/fresh-boot reopen byte audits.
The ordinary C/MASM fixture includes failed DllMain initialization, duplicate
references, unload/reload, existing-thread compiler TLS, callback ordering,
concurrent references/errno, memory allocation failures, actual fault continuation
and caller recovery, event/APC ordering and pending I/O cancellation/close/query
races. Native kernel probes inject every dynamic DLL acquisition failure before
publication and verify absent mappings/TLS plus baseline frame ownership. No
finite suite guarantees absence of every defect. Final cumulative report
reports/runs/host-1792214999674635300-12500/report.json and independent
reports/critics/p10-critic.json passed: 341 host tests, 42 guest cases, both interactive
checks, two matching 16-artifact builds and zero unresolved review findings.

P10 save and fresh-boot reopen each retire 38 threads with zero process-frame
leaks, exercise 103 startup and 35 dynamic-module rollback checkpoints, and
reclaim eight DMA pages. Reopen has zero writes/flushes. Async guest comparison
covers reads, cancellation, close and concurrent result observers; async-write
source was reviewed without a separate unchanged-binary write comparison.
